legal.headline: When Adoption Law Stops at the Border: HAMA, CARA and India’s Expatriate Adoption Lacuna
legal.hook: by Uday Singh Cheema* When Adoption Law Stops at the Border: HAMA, CARA and India’s Expatriate Adoption Lacuna
legal.summary: An analysis of expatriate adoption under HAMA, examining CARA regulations, Hague Convention requirements and cross-border relocation challenges. This article examines the regulatory challenges surrounding expatriate adoptions under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA), analysing the interplay between CARA, the Adoption Regulations, 2022, and the Hague Convention, and proposing a workable framework for cross-border relocation of adopted children. Indian adoption law permits a curious result: an adoption may be complete, valid and irrevocable under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 ( HAMA ), yet encounter no clearly workable regulatory route once the family seeks cross-border relocation.
legal.contextNote: The article discusses the regulatory challenges of expatriate adoption under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA) and the role of the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) in this context. It highlights the issues arising from the Hague Convention on Intercountry Adoption and the Adoption Regulations, 2022. There is no specific case law cited that directly addresses expatriate adoption under HAMA. (1) In-house counsel should review their corporate policies on international adoptions to ensure compliance with CARA guidelines and HAMA provisions. (2) Counsel should assess the implications of the Hague Convention on their cross-border operations, particularly in sectors involving family law or expatriate services. (3) Legal teams should prepare for potential regulatory changes that may arise from ongoing discussions regarding expatriate adoption frameworks.
